title: Saj Bread
description: Saj Bread is a traditional thin Arabic flatbread cooked on a convex griddle called a saj. It is soft, pliable, and slightly blistered, making it ideal for wraps, mezze platters, and serving with grilled meats, labneh, and za’atar.

ingredients.title: Ingredients (makes 8 large rounds)
items: 2 tbsp extra virgin olive oil (plus more for brushing)
1 tsp instant dry yeast (optional, for softer bread – traditional saj can be yeast-free)

instruction.title: Method
steps:
1. Prepare Dough:
• In a large mixing bowl, combine flour, salt, and sugar.
• Make a well, add olive oil, water, and yeast (if using).
• Mix until it forms a shaggy dough.
• Knead 8–10 minutes by hand (or 5 minutes in a stand mixer) until smooth and elastic.

2. Rest & Ferment:
• Place dough in a lightly oiled bowl, cover with a damp cloth.
• Rest 30–45 minutes (yeast dough) or 15 minutes (yeast-free) until supple but not overly airy.

3. Shape:
• Divide dough into 8 equal pieces and roll into smooth balls.
• Cover and rest 10 minutes to relax gluten.
• Roll each ball into a paper-thin circle (30–35 cm wide), as thin as possible.

4. Cook on Saj or Substitute:
• Preheat saj dome or inverted wok/flat griddle to medium-high heat.
• Place dough on surface and smooth quickly with palm or cloth.
• Cook 30–45 seconds per side until blistered with golden spots.
• Transfer to cloth-lined basket and cover to keep soft.

servingSuggestions.title: Serving Suggestions
items: Use for shawarma and grilled meat wraps.
Serve with labneh, hummus, or baba ghanoush.
Pair with za’atar and olive oil.

chefTips: Blend bread flour with 10–15% whole wheat flour for a more authentic texture.
Roll dough extremely thin for traditional saj elasticity.
Keep cooked bread covered in a towel to retain softness and steam.
Work quickly when placing dough on the hot saj to prevent drying.
